sections.title: Added
items: A developer-only tool now watches the controller from outside GameHQ. It is a separate program that only observes - no injection, no hooks, no drivers, no virtual devices - and it is never part of an installed copy. It records, phase by phase, whether the pad still reaches another program through the three Windows input paths, and it says "not measurable" rather than claiming isolation whenever it had nothing to compare against.

sections.title: Changed
items: The exclusive input mode the overlay asks for while it is active is now measured from outside GameHQ instead of being described as unverified. On the test machine, with a controller streaming in the background, another program's controller input stopped while the overlay had the exclusive mode and came back as soon as it was released - twice, in two independent runs. Games that read the controller through other Windows interfaces are unaffected by that mode, which is documented as a limit rather than hidden; the diagnostics keep saying the effect is not verified from inside GameHQ, because that is what they can honestly know.

sections.title: Changed
items: While the in-game overlay is the active window, GameHQ now also asks Windows' GameInput runtime for exclusive foreground input, so other GameInput clients are meant to stop receiving the pad while the overlay is open. The policy has exactly one owner that applies it only after the overlay has really taken the foreground, and releases it again on every way out: closing the overlay, another app taking the focus, the game going away, or GameInput being switched off. Guide and Share handling is unchanged. Whether another program actually stops seeing the pad is not something GameHQ can confirm from inside itself, so the diagnostics report the policy it requested and explicitly do not claim isolation.

sections.title: Changed
items: Opening the in-game overlay now makes it the active window, so the keyboard and the controller drive the overlay instead of the game behind it. The game stays on screen and is never minimised, moved or changed in any way, and closing the overlay hands the focus straight back to it. If Windows refuses to move the focus, the overlay behaves exactly as before and keeps warning that the game may still react to the controller. This is a first step: a game that deliberately reads the controller in the background can still receive it, and that is reported honestly rather than hidden.

sections.title: Added
items: The diagnostic report now records what really happened each time the in-game overlay opened and closed: which window Windows kept in the foreground, whether the game window stayed visible or was minimised, whether GameHQ's own window became active, which controller was serving input and which Windows controller focus policy was in force. This is groundwork for stopping overlay navigation from also reaching the game - it changes no overlay behaviour, and it states plainly that whether the game still receives the controller is not something GameHQ can measure about itself.

sections.title: Changed
items: The Mapping presets section is now three labelled cards - the preset this device runs, the preset being edited, and the preset library - so it is clear at a glance what is assigned and where binding changes are saved. New preset is the only primary button; rename, duplicate and delete moved into a More actions dialog, and a new Assign to this device button makes the preset you are editing the one the controller uses.

sections.title: Changed
items: Mapping presets now sit directly above Assignments on the Input settings page. Choosing the preset a controller or game uses and editing the individual bindings it contains belong together, so the two sections are no longer separated by the profile and gesture settings.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Controllers are identified more precisely. GameHQ now weighs the strongest available evidence about a device first, and when the evidence is ambiguous it keeps controllers separate instead of guessing. Two identical pads connected through one receiver can no longer be treated as a single controller, so their saved bindings stay apart.

sections.title: Fixed
items: The in-game overlay keeps the game in the foreground on every path that opens, moves or raises it. The overlay window is marked as never-activating before it appears, and that mark is restored whenever Windows rebuilds the window, so opening the overlay no longer pulls focus away from a borderless game.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Controller buttons now mean the same thing no matter which Windows input API delivers them. The triggers and stick clicks of a wired DualSense were reported as unnamed buttons by one interface and as named controls by another, so a saved shortcut could stop matching after pressing certain buttons.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Previously discovered updates and their cached release notes remain available after restarting GameHQ offline. Cached discovery never replaces update signature verification.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Added an optional GitHub link beneath upcoming release notes to open the same release in your browser, with controller navigation support.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Upcoming release notes now appear inside GameHQ. Notes in your selected language are fetched from the release on GitHub, with English and cached notes available as fallbacks.

sections.title: Ajouts
items: GameHQ est désormais disponible en seize langues d'interface. Au premier démarrage, il suit la langue de Windows, et vous pouvez en choisir une autre dans les paramètres.
Le changement de langue s'applique immédiatement à toute l'application, y compris la superposition et le menu de la zone de notification, sans redémarrer GameHQ. Votre choix est mémorisé.
Le programme d'installation s'exécute maintenant dans votre langue et transmet ce choix au premier démarrage de GameHQ, si bien que l'installateur et l'application ne se contredisent plus.
L'extension Playnite et les boîtes de dialogue d'erreur du lanceur sont également localisées.
Les nouveautés s'affichent dans votre langue dès qu'une version traduite de ces notes existe. Sinon, c'est le texte anglais complet qui est affiché, jamais un mélange de plusieurs langues.

sections.title: Modifications
items: Les dates, les nombres et les décomptes suivent désormais la langue sélectionnée plutôt que le réglage du système.

sections.title: Limitations connues
items: GameHQ reste une bêta non signée : Windows peut donc signaler un éditeur inconnu au lancement du programme d’installation.
